nodes.name: Corollary 6.9 (equivalences via induced topologies)
nodes.statement: Let ${\cal C}$ be an essentially small category, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a flat functor. Then $F$ induces an equivalence \[ {\cal E}\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J_{F}), \] if and only if $F$ is $J_{F}$-full and the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$
nodes.statement_short: A flat functor induces ${\cal E}\simeq{\bf Sh}({\cal C},J_F)$ iff it is $J_F$-full and its image is separating.
assumptions: ${\cal C}$ be an essentially small category, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a flat functor
conclusions: $F$ induces an equivalence \[ {\cal E}\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J_{F}), \] if and only if $F$ is $J_{F}$-full and the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$
nodes.label: corflatequivalenceinducedtopology

nodes.name: Proposition 6.10 (general setup for equivalences via $J_F$)
nodes.statement: Let $\cal E$ be a Grothendieck topos, represented as the category ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$ of sheaves on a small-generated site $({\cal D}, K)$. Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J_{F}$ the collection of sieves in $\cal C$ whose image under $F$ is $K$-covering. If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$ then $J_{F}$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$, and we have an equivalence of toposes \[ {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J_{F}). \] The following conditions are equivalent to $F$ being a dense (or weakly dense, if $K$ is subcanonical) morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item[(i)'] For any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exists a $K$-covering family of arrows $d_{i}\to d$ whose domains $d_{i}$ are in the image of $F$. \item[(ii)'] For every $c_{1}, c_{2}\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $g:F(c_{1})\to F(c_{2})$ in $\cal D$, there exist a family of arrows $f_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family and a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{2}$ such that $g\circ F(f_{i})=F(k_{i})$ for all $i$. \item[(iii)'] For any arrows $f_{1}, f_{2}:c_{1}\to c_{2}$ in $\cal C$ such that $F(f_1)=F(f_2)$ there exists a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family such that $f_1 \circ k_{i}=f_{2}\circ k_{i}$ for all $i$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: If $F$ is weakly dense from $({\cal C},J_F)$, then $J_F$ is a topology and ${\bf Sh}({\cal D},K)\simeq{\bf Sh}({\cal C},J_F)$; explicit conditions for density.
assumptions: $\cal E$ be a Grothendieck topos, represented as the category ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$ of sheaves on a small-generated site $({\cal D}, K)$. Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J_{F}$ the collection of sieves in $\cal C$ whose image under $F$ is $K$-covering. If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$
conclusions: $J_{F}$ is a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$, and we have an equivalence of toposes \[ {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J_{F}). \] The following conditions are equivalent to $F$ being a dense (or weakly dense, if $K$ is subcanonical) morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J_{F})\to ({\cal D}, K)$: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item[(i)'] For any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exists a $K$-covering family of arrows $d_{i}\to d$ whose domains $d_{i}$ are in the image of $F$. \item[(ii)'] For every $c_{1}, c_{2}\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $g:F(c_{1})\to F(c_{2})$ in $\cal D$, there exist a family of arrows $f_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family and a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{2}$ such that $g\circ F(f_{i})=F(k_{i})$ for all $i$. \item[(iii)'] For any arrows $f_{1}, f_{2}:c_{1}\to c_{2}$ in $\cal C$ such that $F(f_1)=F(f_2)$ there exists a family of arrows $k_{i}:c'_{i}\to c_{1}$ which is sent by $F$ to a $K$-covering family such that $f_1 \circ k_{i}=f_{2}\circ k_{i}$ for all $i$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: propgeneratingequivalence

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.10
nodes.statement: The first part of the proposition follows from Theorem \ref{thmweakdensityequivalence} and Remark \ref{rem1}(a). The second part of the proposition follows from the fact that every dense morphism is weakly dense and that the two notions are equivalent when $K$ is subcanonical.
nodes.statement_short: From Theorem 5.7 and Remark 6.6(a); density and weak density agree for subcanonical $K$.

nodes.name: Image (coinduced) topology $J^F$ (cf. Elephant Lemma C2.3.19(ii))
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. Then there is a Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ on $\cal D$, called the \emph{image of $J$ along $F$} (or the Grothendieck topology \emph{coinduced} by $J$ along $F$), such that for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in J^{F}(d)$ if and only if for any object $c\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$ in $\cal D$, there exists a $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $F(R)\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(T)$. Then the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is $J^{F}$-dense and has the covering-lifting property. The Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ enjoys the following universal property: the subtopos ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, J^{F})\hookrightarrow [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ is the image (in the sense of surjection-inclusion factorization) of the composite of the induced geometric morphism $[F^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]\to [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ with the subtopos inclusion ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$.
nodes.statement_short: $J^F$ on $\cal D$: $T$ covers iff every arrow $F(c)\to d$ pulls it back to contain the image of a $J$-covering sieve; it is the image of the composite subtopos.
assumptions: $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a functor and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$
conclusions: there is a Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ on $\cal D$, called the \emph{image of $J$ along $F$} (or the Grothendieck topology \emph{coinduced} by $J$ along $F$), such that for any sieve $T$ on an object $d$ of $\cal D$, $T\in J^{F}(d)$ if and only if for any object $c\in {\cal C}$ and any arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$ in $\cal D$, there exists a $J$-covering sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $F(R)\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(T)$. Then the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is $J^{F}$-dense and has the covering-lifting property. The Grothendieck topology $J^{F}$ enjoys the following universal property: the subtopos ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, J^{F})\hookrightarrow [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ is the image (in the sense of surjection-inclusion factorization) of the composite of the induced geometric morphism $[F^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]\to [{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ with the subtopos inclusion ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\hookrightarrow [{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$.
nodes.label: propimagetopology

nodes.name: Proof of Image
nodes.statement: First, let us show that $J^{F}$ is indeed a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. The maximality and pullback-stability axiom trivially hold, so it remains to prove the transitivity one. It is clear that any sieve containing a $J^{F}$-covering one is also $J^{F}$-covering. Let us denote, given a sieve $S$ on an object $d$ and, for each arrow $f\in S$, a sieve $S_{f}$ on $\textup{dom}(f)$, by $S\ast \{S_{f} \mid f\in S\}$ the sieve on $d$ consisting of the arrows of the form $f\circ h$ where $f\in S$ and $h\in S_{f}$. We have to prove that, if $S\in J^{F}(d)$ and, for each $f\in S$, $S_{f}\in J^{F}(\textup{dom}(f))$, then $S\ast \{S_{f} \mid f\in S\}\in J^{F}(d)$. Given an arrow $\xi:F(c)\to d$, $F(R) \subseteq \xi^{\ast}(S)$ for some $R\in J(c)$. For any $r\in R$, $\xi \circ F(r)\in S$, so, since $S_{\xi \circ F(r)}\in J^{F}(F(\textup{dom}(r)))$, there is a sieve $R_{r}\in J(\textup{dom}(r))$ such that $F(R_{r})\subseteq S_{\xi \circ F(r)}$. So the $J$-covering sieve $R\ast \{R_{r}\mid r\in R \}$ satisfies the condition $F(R\ast \{R_{r}\mid r\in R \})\subseteq \xi^{\ast}(S\ast \{S_{f} \mid f\in S\})$. The fact that $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is $J^{F}$-dense and has the covering-lifting property is obvious. The last part of the proposition follows at once from Proposition \ref{propsurjectioncomorphismofsites} below. Indeed, the construction of the geometric morphism induced by a comorphism of sites is functorial, the geometric morphism $[G^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]:[{\cal A}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \to [{\cal B}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ induced by a functor $G:{\cal A}\to {\cal B}$ is precisely $L_{G}$, regarding $G$ as a comorphism of sites $({\cal A}, T_{\cal A})\to ({\cal B}, T_{\cal B})$ where $T_{\cal A}$ and $T_{\cal B}$ are the trivial Grothendieck topologies respectively on $\cal A$ and $\cal B$, and any canonical geometric inclusion ${\bf Sh}({\cal A}, Z) \hookrightarrow [{\cal A}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ is induced by the comorphism of sites $1_{\cal A}:({\cal A}, Z) \to ({\cal A}, T)$ given by the identity functor $1_{\cal A}$ on $\cal A$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the topology axioms (transitivity via multicomposition of lifted sieves); the universal property follows from Proposition 7.1 on surjections.

nodes.name: Remark 6.12 ($J^F$ as the largest topology with covering-lifting)
nodes.statement: If $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ satisfies the covering-lifting property then $K\subseteq J^{F}$. This follows immediately from the fact that $K$ satisfies the pullback-stability property. In fact, in Lemma C2.3.19(ii) \cite{El}, $J^{F}$ is characterized as the largest Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ for which $F$ satisfies the covering-lifting property.
nodes.statement_short: Covering-lifting implies $K\subseteq J^F$; $J^F$ is the largest topology for which $F$ has covering-lifting.
nodes.label: remcovlift

nodes.name: Lemma 6.13 (fully faithful functors are cover-reflecting into $J^F$)
nodes.statement: Let $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a $J$-full and $J$-faithful functor, for a Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\cal C$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any sieve $R$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $t$ with codomain $c$, if $F(t)$ belongs to the sieve generated by $F(R)$ then there exists a $J$-covering sieve $U$ on $\textup{dom}(t)$ such that $t\circ u\in R$ for each $u\in U$; \item the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is cover-reflecting. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For $J$-full $J$-faithful $F$, factorizations through $F(R)$ lift locally, and $F:({\cal C},J)\to({\cal D},J^F)$ is cover-reflecting.
assumptions: $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal D}$ be a $J$-full and $J$-faithful functor, for a Grothendieck topology $J$ on $\cal C$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for any sieve $R$ on an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any arrow $t$ with codomain $c$, if $F(t)$ belongs to the sieve generated by $F(R)$
conclusions: there exists a $J$-covering sieve $U$ on $\textup{dom}(t)$ such that $t\circ u\in R$ for each $u\in U$; \item the functor $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, J^{F})$ is cover-reflecting. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lemmafullfaithfulcoverreflecting

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.13
nodes.statement: (i) Suppose that $F(t)=F(r)\circ \xi$ for some $r\in R$, where $t:a\to c$, $r:b\to c$ and $\xi:F(a)\to F(b)$. Since $F$ is $J$-full, there exist a $J$-covering sieve $S$ on $a$ and for each $s\in S$ an arrow $t_{s}:\textup{dom}(s)\to b$ such that $\xi \circ F(s)=F(t_{s})$. Since $F(t)=F(r)\circ \xi$, we have $F(t\circ s)=F(t)\circ F(s)=F(r)\circ \xi \circ F(s)= F(r)\circ F(t_{s})=F(r\circ t_{s})$ for each $s\in S$. The fact that $F$ is $J$-faithful then implies that $t\circ s\equiv_{J} r\circ t_{s}$, that is, there is a $J$-covering sieve $V_{s}$ on $\textup{dom}(s)$ such that for each $v\in V_{s}$, $t\circ s\circ v=r\circ t_{s}\circ v$. Therefore the $J$-covering sieve $U:=S\ast \{V_{s} \mid s\in S\}$ on $a$ satisfies the property that for each $u\in U$, $t\circ u\in R$. (ii) Let $R$ be a sieve on an object $c$ of $\cal C$. If $F(R)$ generates a $J^{F}$-covering sieve then there is a $J$-covering sieve $T$ on $c$ such that the sieve generated by $F(T)$ is contained in the sieve generated by $F(R)$. So, for each $t\in T$, by point (i) of the Lemma, there is a $J$-covering sieve $U_{t}$ on $\textup{dom}(t)$ such that $t\circ u\in R$ for each $u\in U_{t}$. So the sieve $R$ is $J$-covering, since it contains the $J$-covering sieve $T\ast \{U_{t} \mid t\in T\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a factorization by local fullness, then equalize locally by local faithfulness; (ii) by multicomposition.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.14 (generators of a topology recovered along a dense functor)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $K$-dense, cover-preserving and cover-reflecting functor with the covering-lifting property (for instance, a dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ - cf. Corollary \ref{corequivalencecovliftproperty}). Suppose that $K$ is generated by a collection $K'$ of families of arrows which is stable under pullback and such that every $K'$-covering family on an object in the image of $F$ contains the image $F(R)$ under $F$ of some $J$-covering family $R$. If $F$ is $J'$-full and $J'$-faithful, where $J'$ is the Grothendieck topology generated by the sieves $R$ such that $F(R)\in K'$, then $J=J'$.
nodes.statement_short: If $K$ is generated by a pullback-stable $K'$ lifting to $J$-covers, and $F$ is $J'$-full and $J'$-faithful, then $J$ equals the topology $J'$ generated by the lifted sieves.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a $K$-dense, cover-preserving and cover-reflecting functor with the covering-lifting property (for instance, a dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ - cf. Corollary \ref{corequivalencecovliftproperty}). Suppose that $K$ is generated by a collection $K'$ of families of arrows which is stable under pullback and such that every $K'$-covering family on an object in the image of $F$ contains the image $F(R)$ under $F$ of some $J$-covering family $R$. If $F$ is $J'$-full and $J'$-faithful, where $J'$ is the Grothendieck topology generated by the sieves $R$ such that $F(R)\in K'$,
nodes.label: corliftinggeneration

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.14
nodes.statement: Let $J'$ be the Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$ generated by the sieves $R$ such that $F(R)$ generates a $K$-covering sieve. We have to prove that $J'=J$. Consider the topology $J'^{F}$. We clearly have $K'\subseteq J'^{F}$, whence $K\subseteq J'^{F}$. On the other hand, $K=J^{F}$ by Proposition \ref{proprecoverytopology}. Now, the fact that $F$ is cover-reflecting implies that $J'\subseteq J$; so $J'^{F}\subseteq J^{F}=K$, and hence $J'^{F}=K$. Now, since both $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ and $F:({\cal C}, J')\to ({\cal D}, J'^{F})$ are cover-reflecting (the former by our hypothesis and the latter by Lemma \ref{lemmafullfaithfulcoverreflecting}), $J'^{F}=K$ implies that $J=J'$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare coinduced topologies: $K\subseteq J'^F\subseteq J^F=K$, then use cover-reflection of both functors (Lemma 6.13).

nodes.name: Remark 6.15 (necessity of local fullness and faithfulness)
nodes.statement: If $F$ is a weakly dense morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$, the condition that $F$ be $J'$-full and $J'$-faithful is also necessary for $J$ to be equal to $J'$ (see Proposition \ref{propmorphismcomorphismequivalence}).
nodes.statement_short: For weakly dense $F$ the $J'$-fullness and faithfulness are also necessary.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.16
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{corliftinggeneration} has the following immediate corollary, which allows to obtain, from a set of generators of a Grothendieck topology, a set of generators for a topology induced by it on a full dense subcategory.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Theorem 6.14.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.16 (generators of induced topologies on dense subcategories)
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal D}, K)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal C$ a full $K$-dense subcategory of $\cal D$ and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. Suppose that $K$ is generated by a collection $K'$ of families of arrows which is stable under pullback and such that every $K'$-covering family on an object in $\cal C$ is refined by a $J$-covering family. Then $J$ is generated by the families in $K'$ whose arrows lie all in $\cal C$.
nodes.statement_short: If $K$ is generated by pullback-stable families refined by $J$-covers, then $J$ is generated by the families of $K'$ lying in $\cal C$.
assumptions: $({\cal D}, K)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal C$ a full $K$-dense subcategory of $\cal D$ and $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $\cal C$. Suppose that $K$ is generated by a collection $K'$ of families of arrows which is stable under pullback and such that every $K'$-covering family on an object in $\cal C$ is refined by a $J$-covering family
conclusions: $J$ is generated by the families in $K'$ whose arrows lie all in $\cal C$.
nodes.label: corgensep

nodes.name: Corollary 6.17 (intrinsic characterization of geometric inclusions)
nodes.statement: Let $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be a geometric morphism. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $f$ is an inclusion if and only if $f^{\ast}$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item \textup{$f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective}, that is every object of $\cal F$ can be covered by objects in the image of $f^{\ast}$; \item \textup{$f^{\ast}$ is locally full}, that is for every $x, y\in {\cal E}$ and any arrow $g:f^{\ast}(x)\to f^{\ast}(y)$ in $\cal F$, there exists a family of arrows $s_{i}:x_{i}\to x$ in $\cal E$ which is sent by $f^{\ast}$ to an epimorphic family and a family of arrows $g_{i}:x_{i}\to y$ such that $g\circ f^{\ast}(s_{i})=f^{\ast}(g_{i})$ for all $i$. \end{enumerate} \item $f$ is an equivalence if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful, locally full and locally surjective. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is an inclusion iff $f^*$ is locally surjective and locally full; an equivalence iff moreover faithful.
assumptions: $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be a geometric morphism
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $f$ is an inclusion if and only if $f^{\ast}$ satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item \textup{$f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective}, that is every object of $\cal F$ can be covered by objects in the image of $f^{\ast}$; \item \textup{$f^{\ast}$ is locally full}, that is for every $x, y\in {\cal E}$ and any arrow $g:f^{\ast}(x)\to f^{\ast}(y)$ in $\cal F$, there exists a family of arrows $s_{i}:x_{i}\to x$ in $\cal E$ which is sent by $f^{\ast}$ to an epimorphic family and a family of arrows $g_{i}:x_{i}\to y$ such that $g\circ f^{\ast}(s_{i})=f^{\ast}(g_{i})$ for all $i$. \end{enumerate} \item $f$ is an equivalence if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful, locally full and locally surjective. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corinclusionequivalence

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.17
nodes.statement: (i) The above conditions amount precisely to the property of the morphism of sites $({\cal E}, {J_{\cal E}^{\textup{can}}}_{f^{\ast}})\to ({\cal F}, J_{\cal F}^{\textup{can}})$ to be dense, so the thesis follows from Theorem \ref{Morphismsmaalgenerated}. (ii) This follows from (i), given that a geometric morphism is an equivalence if and only if it is a surjection and an inclusion.
nodes.statement_short: The conditions express density of the morphism of sites $f^*$; apply Theorem 6.3; equivalence = surjection and inclusion.

nodes.name: Remark 6.18 (single-arrow covers suffice)
nodes.statement: Since a Grothendieck topos has all coproducts, all the covering families arising in the formulations of the properties in part (i) of Corollary \ref{corinclusionequivalence} can be supposed, without loss of generality, to consist of a single element. More precisely, the condition for $f$ to be an inclusion is equivalent to the conjunction of the following ones: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item every object of $\cal F$ is a quotient of an object in the image of $f^{\ast}$; \item for every $x, y\in {\cal E}$ and any arrow $g:f^{\ast}(x)\to f^{\ast}(y)$ in $\cal F$, there exist an arrow $s:x'\to x$ in $\cal E$ which is sent by $f^{\ast}$ to an epimorphism and an arrow $g':x'\to y$ such that $g\circ f^{\ast}(s)=f^{\ast}(g')$. \end{enumerate} So, $f$ is an equivalence if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful and satisfies the above conditions.
nodes.statement_short: Using coproducts, local surjectivity and fullness can be stated with single epimorphisms.
nodes.label: remsurjectionsinclusions

nodes.name: Example 6.19 (slices of inclusions are inclusions)
nodes.statement: Let $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be a geometric morphism between Grothendieck toposes and $A$ an object of $\cal E$. Then we have a geometric morphism $f_{A}:{\cal F}\slash f^{\ast}(A)\to {\cal E}\slash A$ such that the diagram $$ \xymatrix{ {\cal F}\slash f^{\ast}(A) \ar[r] \ar[d]_{f_{A}} & {\cal F} \ar[d]^{f} \\ {\cal E}\slash A \ar[r] & {\cal E} } $$ where the horizontal morphisms are the canonical ones, commutes. The inverse image of $f_{A}$ is the functor ${\cal E}\slash A \to {\cal F}\slash f^{\ast}(A)$ sending an object $u:B\to A$ of ${\cal E}\slash A$ to $f^{\ast}(u):f^{\ast}(B)\to f^{\ast}(A)$ (and acting accordingly on arrows). Let us show, by applying Corollary \ref{corinclusionequivalence}(i), that if $f$ is an inclusion then $f_{A}$ is also an inclusion. First, let us show that ${f_{A}}^{\ast}$ is locally surjective. Given an object $u:C\to f^{\ast}(A)$ of ${\cal F}\slash f^{\ast}(A)$, since $f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective there is an object $B$ of $\cal E$ and an epimorphism $q:f^{\ast}(B)\to C$. Consider the composite arrow $u\circ q:f^{\ast}(B)\to f^{\ast}(A)$. Since $f^{\ast}$ satisfies condition (ii) of Corollary \ref{corinclusionequivalence}(i), there is an arrow $s:B'\to B$ in $\cal E$ and an arrow $g:B'\to A$ in $\cal E$ such that $f^{\ast}(s)$ is an epimorphism and $u\circ q\circ f^{\ast}(s)=f^{\ast}(g)$ (cf. Remark \ref{remsurjectionsinclusions}). Therefore the arrow $q\circ f^{\ast}(s)$ is an epimorphism from ${f_{A}}^{\ast}(g)$ to $u$ in ${\cal F}\slash f^{\ast}(A)$. The fact that ${f_{A}}^{\ast}$ inherits local fullness from $f^{\ast}$ is obvious.
nodes.statement_short: If $f$ is an inclusion then so is $f_A:{\cal F}/f^*(A)\to{\cal E}/A$, by Corollary 6.17.
nodes.label: exgeometricinclusion

nodes.name: Hyperconnected and localic geometric morphisms
nodes.statement: Recall that a geometric morphism $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ is said to be \emph{hyperconnected} if $f^{\ast}$ is full and faithful and its image is closed under subobjects in $\cal F$, and is said to be \emph{localic} if every object of $\cal F$ is a subquotient (that is, a quotient of a subobject) of an object of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A\in {\cal E}$.

nodes.name: Hyperconnected-localic factorization (Elephant A4.6.5)
nodes.statement: By Theorem A4.6.5 \cite{El}, every geometric morphism can be factored, uniquely up to commuting equivalence, as the composite of a hyperconnected morphism followed by a localic one.
nodes.statement_short: Every geometric morphism factors uniquely as a hyperconnected morphism followed by a localic one.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.20 (pullback of a coequalizer along a mono)
nodes.statement: Let $q:X\to X'$ be the coequalizer of a pair of arrows $r_{1}, r_{2}:R\to X$ in a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:Y\to X'$ a monomorphism. Then, the arrows $t_{1}, t_{2}:R\times_{X'} Y \to Z$ which make the diagram $$ \xymatrix{ R\times_{X'} Y \ar@<-.5ex>[d]_{t_{1}} \ar@<.5ex>[d]^{t_{2}} \ar[rr] & & R \ar@<-.5ex>[d]_{r_{1}} \ar@<.5ex>[d]^{r_{2}} \\ Z \ar[d]^{k} \ar[rr]^{h} & & X \ar[d]^{q} \\ Y \ar[rr]^{f} & & X' } $$ commutative, where the bottom square is a pullback, satisfy the property that $\langle t_{1}, t_{2}\rangle :R\times_{X'} Y \to Z\times Z$ is (isomorphic to) the pullback of $\langle r_{1}, r_{2} \rangle $ along $h\times h$. Moreover, $k$ is the coequalizer of the arrows $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pulling back a coequalizer along a monomorphism yields a coequalizer whose kernel pair is the pullback of the original one.
assumptions: $q:X\to X'$ be the coequalizer of a pair of arrows $r_{1}, r_{2}:R\to X$ in a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:Y\to X'$ a monomorphism
conclusions: the arrows $t_{1}, t_{2}:R\times_{X'} Y \to Z$ which make the diagram $$ \xymatrix{ R\times_{X'} Y \ar@<-.5ex>[d]_{t_{1}} \ar@<.5ex>[d]^{t_{2}} \ar[rr] & & R \ar@<-.5ex>[d]_{r_{1}} \ar@<.5ex>[d]^{r_{2}} \\ Z \ar[d]^{k} \ar[rr]^{h} & & X \ar[d]^{q} \\ Y \ar[rr]^{f} & & X' } $$ commutative, where the bottom square is a pullback, satisfy the property that $\langle t_{1}, t_{2}\rangle :R\times_{X'} Y \to Z\times Z$ is (isomorphic to) the pullback of $\langle r_{1}, r_{2} \rangle $ along $h\times h$. Moreover, $k$ is the coequalizer of the arrows $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$.
nodes.label: lempb

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.20
nodes.statement: By using the internal language, we shall argue as if $\cal E$ were the topos ${\bf Set }$ of sets. Let $U\to Z\times Z$ be the pullback of $\langle r_{1}, r_{2} \rangle $ along $h\times h$. We have \[ U=\{ ((z_{1}, z_{2}), \xi) \mid (z_{1}, z_{2})\in Z, \, \xi\in R, \, h(z_{1})=r_{1}(\xi), \, h(z_{2})=r_{2}(\xi) \}. \] We want to prove that $U\to Z\times Z$ is isomorphic to $\langle t_{1}, t_{2}\rangle\,:R\times_{X'} Y \to Z\times Z$ as arrows over $Z\times Z$. We have $$R\times_{X'} Y=\{(\xi, y) \mid \xi \in R, \, y\in Y, \, q(r_{1}(\xi))=q(r_{2}(\xi))=f(y) \}.$$ Now, the arrow $t_{1}:R\times_{X'} Y \to Z$ (resp. $t_{2}:R\times_{X'} Y \to Z$) sends an element $(\xi, y)\in R\times_{X'} Y$ to the unique element $z_{1}\in Z$ such that $k(z_{1})=y$ and $h(z_{1})=r_{1}(\xi)$ (resp. to the unique element $z_{2}\in Z$ such that $k(z_{2})=y$ and $h(z_{2})=r_{2}(\xi)$). Let us define arrows $R\times_{X'} Y \to U$ and $U \to R\times_{X'} Y$ over $Z\times Z$ that are inverse to each other. In one direction, we send an element $(\xi, y)\in R\times_{X'} Y$ to the element $(t_{1}(\xi, y), t_{2}(\xi, y), \xi)$. This is well-defined by definition of the arrows $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$. In the converse direction, we observe that, given an element $((z_{1}, z_{2}), \xi) $ of $U$, we have $k(z_{1})=k(z_{2})$. Indeed, since $f$ is monic, this condition is equivalent to $f(k(z_{1}))=f(k(z_{2}))$; but $f(k(z_{1}))=q(h(z_{1}))=q(r_{1}(\xi))=q(r_{2}(\xi))=q(h(z_{2}))=f(k(z_{2}))$. We can therefore define an arrow $U\to R\times_{X'} Y$ which sends an element $((z_{1}, z_{2}), \xi) $ of $U$ to the element $(\xi, k(z_{1}))$. This is well-defined since $q(r_{1}(\xi))=q(h(z_{1}))=f(k(z_{1}))$ and $q(r_{2}(\xi))=q(h(z_{2}))=f(k(z_{2}))=f(k(z_{1}))$ (as $k(z_{1})=k(z_{2})$). It is now straightforward to check that the two arrows just defined are inverse to each other and compatible with the structure arrows to $Z\times Z$. This completes the proof of the first part of the lemma. The fact that $k$ is the coequalizer of the arrows $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ follows from the fact that in a Grothendieck topos colimits are stable under pullback.
nodes.statement_short: Argue in the internal language as in ${\bf Set}$: construct mutually inverse maps between the two pullbacks; coequalizer by pullback-stability of colimits.

nodes.name: Remark 6.21 (general version of the lemma)
nodes.statement: The proof of the lemma shows that the general version of it (for $f$ not necessarily monic) reads as follows: $\langle t_{1}, t_{2}\rangle$ is isomorphic over $Z\times Z$ to the composite with the canonical embedding $z_{Y}:Z\times_{Y} Z \hookrightarrow Z\times Z$ of the pullback of $\langle r_{1}, r_{2} \rangle $ along $(h\times h)\circ z_{Y}$.
nodes.statement_short: For non-monic $f$, the kernel pair is a pullback restricted to $Z\times_Y Z$.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.22 (closure under subobjects tested on a separating set)
nodes.statement: Let ${\cal C}$ be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism. Then the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, every subobject of $f^{\ast}(c)$ is in the image of $f^{\ast}$.
nodes.statement_short: The image of $f^*$ is closed under subobjects iff subobjects of $f^*(c)$, for $c$ in a separating set, are in the image.
assumptions: ${\cal C}$ be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism
conclusions: the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects if and only if for any $c\in {\cal C}$, every subobject of $f^{\ast}(c)$ is in the image of $f^{\ast}$.
nodes.label: prophypersubobjects

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.22
nodes.statement: Let $m:B\rightarrowtail f^{\ast}(A)$ be a monomorphism. Let us represent $A$ as a quotient $q:\coprod_{c\in {\cal C}_{A}}c\to A$ of a coproduct of objects coming from $\cal C$. Then, since the image of $f^{\ast}|_{\cal C}$ is closed under subobjects and coproducts are stable under pullbacks, the pullback of $m$ along $f^{\ast}(q)$ is of the form $f^{\ast}(z)$ for some subobject $z:Z\rightarrowtail \coprod_{c\in {\cal C}_{A}}c$ in $\cal E$. Now, if $q$ is the coequalizer of its kernel pair $\langle r_{1},r_{2} \rangle $ in $\cal E$ then $f^{\ast}(q)$ is the coequalizer of the pair $f^{\ast}(r_{1}), f^{\ast}(r_{2})$. Let $\langle t_{1}, t_{2}\rangle:T\to Z$ be the pullback in $\cal E$ of $\langle r_{1}, r_{2}\rangle $ along $z$. Then, since $f^{\ast}$ preserves pullbacks, $\langle f^{\ast}(t_{1}), f^{\ast}(t_{2})\rangle:f^{\ast}(T)\to f^{\ast}(Z)$ is the pullback of $\langle f^{\ast}(r_{1}), f^{\ast}(r_{2})\rangle $ along $f^{\ast}(z)$. By Lemma \ref{lempb}, it follows that $m$ is isomorphic to the canonical arrow $U \to f^{\ast}(A)$ from the codomain $U$ of the coequalizer $f^{\ast}(Z)\to U$ of the arrows $f^{\ast}(t_{1}), f^{\ast}(t_{2})$. But, since $f^{\ast}$ preserves coequalizers, this arrow is the image under $f^{\ast}$ of the canonical arrow $\xi:Z_{T} \to A$ from the codomain $Z_{T}$ of the coequalizer $Z\to Z_{T}$ of the two arrows $t_{1}, t_{2}$ to $A$, that is, $m\cong \textup{Im}(f^{\ast}(\xi))\cong f^{\ast}(\textup{Im}(\xi))$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover $A$ by a coproduct of separating objects, pull back the subobject, and use Lemma 6.20 to express it as an image of $f^*$.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.23 (hyperconnected morphisms induced by flat functors)
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor. Then the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and for every subobject $A\rightarrowtail F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is hyperconnected iff $F$ is cover-reflecting and every subobject of $F(c)$ is a union of images of arrows of a sieve on $c$.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor
conclusions: the geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and for every subobject $A\rightarrowtail F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.label: prophyperconnected

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.23
nodes.statement: It is clear that if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful and its image is closed under subobjects then $f^{\ast}$ is also full (see the proof of the implication (vi) $\!\Rightarrow\!$ (i) at p. 229 of \cite{El}). So it follows from Propositions \ref{propcoverreflecting} and \ref{prophypersubobjects} that $f$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and, for every object $c$ of $\cal C$, all the subobjects of $f^{\ast}(l(c))$ are images under $f^{\ast}$ of subobjects of $l(c)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. Now, since the subobjects of $l(c)$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ are all images under the associated sheaf functor $a_{J}:[{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }] \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J) $ of subobjects of the form $R \rightarrowtail {\rm Hom}_{\cal C}(-,c)$ (which can be supposed $J$-closed without loss of generality), and this subobject is the union of the images of the arrows of the form $y_{\cal C}(f)$ for $f\in R$ (where $y_{\cal C}$ is the Yoneda embedding), we can reformulate the latter condition as the requirement that for any object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any subobject $A\rightarrowtail F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there should exist a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.statement_short: Faithful plus closure under subobjects gives fullness; apply Propositions 6.1 and 6.22 and describe subobjects of $l(c)$ by sieves.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.24 (interpretations inducing hyperconnected morphisms)
nodes.statement: An interpretation $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ between geometric theories $\mathbb T$ and $\mathbb S$ induces an hyperconnected geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ if and only if for every sequent $\sigma$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$, if the sequent $I(\sigma)$ is provable in $\mathbb S$ then $\sigma$ is provable in $\mathbb T$, and for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula $I(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a geometric formula over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$. In particular, if $I$ is the canonical interpretation given by an expansion ${\mathbb T}'$ of ${\mathbb T}$ (in the sense of section 7.1 of \cite{OCBook}) then the geometric morphism induced by $I$ is hyperconnected if and only if every sequent over the signature of $\mathbb T$ which is provable in ${\mathbb T}'$ is provable in $\mathbb T$, and for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$ over the signature of ${\mathbb T}'$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a geometric formula over the signature of $\mathbb T$.
nodes.statement_short: An interpretation induces a hyperconnected morphism iff it reflects provability and every formula in an image context is equivalent to an image formula.
nodes.label: corsyntactichyperconnected

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.24
nodes.statement: Our thesis follows immediately from Proposition \ref{prophyperconnected} in light of Corollary \ref{corinterpretationsfaithful}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 6.23 with Corollary 6.2.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.25 (hyperconnected morphisms from morphisms of sites)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and \emph{closed-sieve-lifting}, in the sense that for every object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any $K$-closed sieve $S$ on $F(c)$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $S$ coincides with the ($K$-closed) sieve on $F(c)$ generated by the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.statement_short: ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is hyperconnected iff $F$ is cover-reflecting and closed-sieve-lifting.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is hyperconnected if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting and \emph{closed-sieve-lifting}, in the sense that for every object $c$ of $\cal C$ and any $K$-closed sieve $S$ on $F(c)$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $S$ coincides with the ($K$-closed) sieve on $F(c)$ generated by the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$.
nodes.label: prophyperconnectedsites

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.25
nodes.statement: The thesis follows as an immediate consequence of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnected} in light of Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects}. Indeed, the condition of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnected} amounts precisely to the requirement that for every subobject $A\rightarrowtail l'(F(c))$, where $l'$ is the canonical functor ${\cal D}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$, there should be a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $l'(F(f))$ for $f\in R$. Now, the subobjects of $l'(F(c))$ in ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$ are the images under the associated sheaf functor $a_{K}:[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]\to {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$ of $K$-closed sieves $S$ on $F(c)$, and the union of the images of the arrows $l'(F(f))$ for $f\in R$ is the image under $a_{K}$ of the union of the images of the arrows $y_{\cal D}(F(f))$ for $f\in R$; our claim thus follows from the fact that, by Proposition \ref{propclosedsubobjects}, two subobjects of a given object in $[{\cal D}^{\textup{op}}, {\bf Set }]$ have isomorphic images under $a_{K}$ if and only if their $K$-closures coincide.
nodes.statement_short: Translate the subobject condition of Proposition 6.23 via Proposition 2.3 into closed sieves.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.26 (essential surjectivity of inverse images)
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. If the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects then $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective if and only if the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.
nodes.statement_short: If the image of $f^*$ is closed under subobjects, $f^*$ is essentially surjective iff the objects $F(c)$ are separating.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. If the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects
conclusions: $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective if and only if the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.
nodes.label: propessentiallysurjective

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.26
nodes.statement: If the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set of objects for $\cal E$ then for every $A\in {\cal E}$, we have an epimorphism $q:f^{\ast}(\coprod_{i\in I}l(c_{i}))\cong \coprod_{i\in I}f^{\ast}(l(c_{i}))\twoheadrightarrow A$. Since the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects, the kernel pair of $q$ is of the form $f^{\ast}(R)$, where $R$ is a relation on $\coprod_{i\in I}l(c_{i})$. Then $q$ is isomorphic to the image under $f^{\ast}$ of the coequalizer of $R$; in particular, $A$ is isomorphic to an object in the image of $f^{\ast}$, as desired. Conversely, if $f^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective then for every object $A$ of $\cal E$, there exists an object $B$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ such that $A\cong f^{\ast}(B)$. But $B$ can be covered in ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ by objects of the form $l(c)$ for $\cal C$, whence $A$ can be covered in $\cal E$ by objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Separating images give quotient presentations whose kernel pairs lie in the image; conversely objects of the sheaf topos are covered by representables.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.27 (interpretations: essential surjectivity and closure under subobjects)
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ satisfies the property that its inverse image is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if for every sort $B$ of the signature of $\mathbb S$, the object $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$ and the image of $I$ is closed under subobjects (that is, for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula $I(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a geometric formula over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$).
nodes.statement_short: The inverse image is essentially surjective with subobject-closed image iff sorts are covered by images and the image is closed under subobjects.
assumptions: $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ satisfies the property that its inverse image is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if for every sort $B$ of the signature of $\mathbb S$, the object $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$ and the image of $I$ is closed under subobjects (that is, for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula $I(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a geometric formula over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$).

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.27
nodes.statement: By Propositions \ref{prophypersubobjects} and \ref{propessentiallysurjective}, since the geometric syntactic category ${\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ is closed under subobjects in the topos ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}_{\mathbb S}, J_{\mathbb S})$, it suffices to show, assuming that the image of $I$ is closed under subobjects, that the objects in the image of $I$ form a separating set for the topos ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]$ if and only if every object of the form $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ (for $B$ a sort of the signature of $\mathbb S$) is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$. But this follows from the fact that every object of ${\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ is a subobject of a finite product of objects of the form $\{x^{B}. \top\}$, using the fact that $I$ preserves finite products and its image is closed under subobjects.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Propositions 6.22 and 6.26 using that syntactic objects are subobjects of products of sorts.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.28 (essential surjectivity via morphisms of sites)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ satisfies the property that ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting (in the sense of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnectedsites}) and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} (equivalently, if $K$ is subcanonical, every object of $\cal D$ admits a $K$-covering sieve generated by arrows whose domain lies in the image of $F$).
nodes.statement_short: ${\bf Sh}(F)^*$ is essentially surjective with subobject-closed image iff $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition 5.5.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ satisfies the property that ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}$ is essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects if and only if $F$ is closed-sieve-lifting (in the sense of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnectedsites}) and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} (equivalently, if $K$ is subcanonical, every object of $\cal D$ admits a $K$-covering sieve generated by arrows whose domain lies in the image of $F$).
nodes.label: propessentialsurjectivitysites

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.28
nodes.statement: The equivalence between the property of the image of ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}$ to be closed under subobjects and the property of $F$ to be closed-sieve-lifting follows from the proof of Proposition \ref{prophyperconnectedsites}, while the equivalence between the property of ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}$ to be essentially surjective and condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} follows from the proof of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism}.
nodes.statement_short: From the proofs of Propositions 6.25 and 5.5.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.29 (localic morphisms and separating sets)
nodes.statement: Let ${\cal C}$ (resp. $\cal D$) be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ (resp. $\cal F$) and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism. Then: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The full subcategory $\cal G$ of $\cal F$ on the objects which are subquotients of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A\in {\cal E}$ coincides with the full subcategory of $\cal F$ on the objects which can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \item $f$ is localic if and only if every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Subquotients of objects $f^*(A)$ are those covered by subobjects of $f^*(c)$ for $c$ separating; $f$ is localic iff the separating set of $\cal F$ is so covered.
assumptions: ${\cal C}$ (resp. $\cal D$) be a separating set for a Grothendieck topos $\cal E$ (resp. $\cal F$) and $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ a geometric morphism
conclusions: Then: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The full subcategory $\cal G$ of $\cal F$ on the objects which are subquotients of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A\in {\cal E}$ coincides with the full subcategory of $\cal F$ on the objects which can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \item $f$ is localic if and only if every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: proplocalic

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.29
nodes.statement: (i) Let $B\in {\cal G}$. Then $B$ is a quotient $d\to B$ of a subobject $d\rightarrowtail f^{\ast}(A)$. But $A$ is a quotient $q:\coprod_{i\in I}c_{i}\to A$ of a coproduct of objects $c_{i}$ in $\cal C$, so, by considering the pullback \[ \xymatrix{ d' \ar[d] \ar[r] & f^{\ast}(\coprod_{i\in I}c_{i})\cong \coprod_{i\in I}f^{\ast}(c_i) \ar[d]^{q} \\ d \ar[r] & f^{\ast}(A) } \] we see that $B$ is a quotient of $d'$, which is a coproduct of subobjects of the objects $f^{\ast}(c_i)$. Therefore $B$ can be covered by the domains of these subobjects, as required. Conversely, let us suppose that $B$ is an object of $\cal F$ that can be covered by objects $u_{i}$ (for $i\in I$) which are domains of subobjects $u_{i} \rightarrowtail f^{\ast}(c_{i})$ of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(c_{i})$ for $c_{i}$ in $\cal C$. Then $B$ is a quotient of the coproduct of the $u_{i}$ (for $i\in I$), which is a subobject of the coproduct of the $f^{\ast}(c_{i})$; but this coproduct is in the image of $f^{\ast}$ as $f^{\ast}$ preserves coproducts. (ii) By definition of a localic morphism, $f$ is localic if and only if ${\cal G}={\cal F}$. So, by point (i), if $f$ is localic then every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$. Conversely, again by (i), we have to prove that if every object of $\cal D$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$ then every object of $\cal F$ can be covered by objects which are domains of subobjects of objects of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A$ in $\cal C$; but this immediately follows from the fact that $\cal D$ is separating for $\cal F$.
nodes.statement_short: Pull back along a coproduct cover to show subquotients are covered by subobjects of $f^*(c_i)$, and conversely; (ii) follows using that $\cal D$ is separating.

nodes.name: Remark 6.30 (separating set of the localic part)
nodes.statement: We know from section A4.6 of \cite{El} that if $\cal E$ and $\cal F$ are Grothendieck toposes then the category $\cal G$ defined in point (i) of Proposition \ref{proplocalic} is a Grothendieck topos; so this part of the proposition actually asserts that the collection of objects which are subobjects of an object of the form $f^{\ast}(A)$ for $A\in {\cal C}$ is a separating set for $\cal G$.
nodes.statement_short: The subobjects of objects $f^*(A)$ form a separating set of the intermediate topos $\cal G$.
nodes.label: remseparatingsetlocalic

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.31
nodes.statement: The following result is an immediate corollary of Proposition \ref{proplocalic}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Proposition 6.29.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.31 (localic morphisms induced by flat functors)
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. Then $f$ is localic if and only if the subobjects of objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is localic iff subobjects of objects $F(c)$ form a separating set.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: $f$ is localic if and only if the subobjects of objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$.

nodes.name: Proposition 6.32 (localic morphisms from morphisms of sites)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is localic if and only if for any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exist a family $\{S_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of sieves on objects of the form $F(c_{i})$ (where $c_{i}$ is an object of $\cal C$) and for each $f\in S_{i}$ an arrow $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ such that $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, such that the family of arrows $g_{f}$ (for $f\in S_{i}$ for some $i$) is $K$-covering.
nodes.statement_short: ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is localic iff every object of $\cal D$ is $K$-covered by compatible families indexed by sieves on objects $F(c_i)$.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is localic if and only if for any object $d$ of $\cal D$ there exist a family $\{S_{i} \mid i\in I\}$ of sieves on objects of the form $F(c_{i})$ (where $c_{i}$ is an object of $\cal C$) and for each $f\in S_{i}$ an arrow $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ such that $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$, such that the family of arrows $g_{f}$ (for $f\in S_{i}$ for some $i$) is $K$-covering.
nodes.label: proplocalicsites

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.32
nodes.statement: Let us suppose that ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is localic. Let $l'$ be the canonical functor ${\cal D}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$. By Proposition \ref{proplocalic}, for every $d\in {\cal D}$ there exist objects $c_{i}$ of $\cal C$ (for $i\in I$), subobjects $A_{i}\rightarrowtail l'(F(c_i))$ and a jointly epimorphic family of arrows $A_{i}\to l'(d)$ (for $i\in I$). Now, we can write $A_{i}=a_{K}(S_{i})$, where $S_i$ is a sieve on $F(c_i)$. For each $f\in S_{i}$, composing the arrow $a_{K}(S_{i})\to l'(d)$ with the canonical arrow $l'(\textup{dom}(f))\to a_{K}(S_{i})$ thus yields an arrow $l'(\textup{dom}(f))\to l'(d)$ which we can suppose without loss of generality of the form $l'(g_{f})$ for an arrow $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ (at the cost of replacing $S_{i}$, by using Proposition \ref{propexplicit}, which a smaller sieve with the same image under $a_{K}$); clearly, for any $z$ composable with $f$, $l'(g_{f\circ z})=l'(g_{f}\circ z)$, equivalently $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$. The property of our arrows $A_{i}\to l'(d)$ to be jointly epimorphic can thus be reformulated as the property of the arrows $g_{f}$ to be sent by $l'$ to an epimorphic family, equivalently to be $K$-covering. Conversely, any family of arrows $g_{f}:\textup{dom}(f)\to d$ indexed by a sieve $S_{i}$ such that $g_{f\circ z}\equiv_{K} g_{f}\circ z$ whenever $z$ is composable with $f$ induces an arrow $a_K(S_i)\to l'(d)$. So if we have a family of sieves $S_{i}$ on objects of the form $F(c_i)$ and one such family of arrows for each sieve, the resulting arrows $a_K(S_i)\to l'(d)$ will be jointly epimorphic if (and only if) the family of arrows $g_{f}$ (for $f\in S_{i}$ for some $i$) is $K$-covering.
nodes.statement_short: Write subobjects of $l'(F(c))$ as $a_K(S)$ and represent arrows from them locally (Proposition 2.5).

nodes.name: Proposition 6.33 (interpretations inducing localic morphisms)
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ is localic if and only if every object of ${\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ can be $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by formulae over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in a context of the form $I(\vec{x})$ which $\mathbb T$-provably entail a formula of the form $I(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a geometric formula in the context $\vec{x}$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$. In particular, the canonical interpretation of $\mathbb T$ into an expansion of it over a signature which does not contain any new sorts with respect to the signature of $\mathbb T$ induces a localic geometric morphism.
nodes.statement_short: An interpretation induces a localic morphism iff objects are covered by formulae entailing image formulae; expansions without new sorts are localic.
assumptions: $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ is localic if and only if every object of ${\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ can be $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by formulae over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in a context of the form $I(\vec{x})$ which $\mathbb T$-provably entail a formula of the form $I(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a geometric formula in the context $\vec{x}$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$. In particular, the canonical interpretation of $\mathbb T$ into an expansion of it over a signature which does not contain any new sorts with respect to the signature of $\mathbb T$ induces a localic geometric morphism.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.33
nodes.statement: This is an immediate consequence of Proposition \ref{proplocalic}, by using the fact that the subobjects in ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}_{\mathbb S}, J_{\mathbb S})$ of an object of the form $I(\{\vec{x}. \phi\})$ for a geometric formula-in-context $\phi(\vec{x})$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ can be identified with the ($\mathbb S$-provable equivalence classes of) geometric formulae in the context $I(\vec{x})$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ which $\mathbb S$-provably entail $I(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 6.29, identifying subobjects of $I(\{\vec x.\phi\})$ with formulae entailing $I(\phi)$.

nodes.name: Topology $C^s_J$ on ${\cal C}^s_J$
nodes.statement: Let $C_{J}^{s}$ be the Grothendieck topology induced on ${\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ by the canonical topology on the topos ${\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$.

nodes.name: Canonical morphism of sites $i^s_J$
nodes.statement: We have a canonical functor ${\cal C}\to {\cal C}_{J}^{s}$ sending an object $c$ of $\cal C$ to the pair $(c, M_{c})$, where $M_{c}$ is the maximal sieve on $c$, which yields a morphism of sites $i_{J}^{s}:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal C}_{J}^{s}, C_{J}^{s})$.

nodes.name: $i^s_J$ induces an equivalence
nodes.statement: This morphism induces an equivalence ${\bf Sh}(i_{J}^{s}):{\bf Sh}({\cal C}_{J}^{s}, C_{J}^{s}) \simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical morphism of sites $i^s_J$ induces an equivalence of toposes.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.34 (site-level hyperconnected-localic factorization)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the hyperconnected-localic factorization of the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F)\circ {\bf Sh}(i_{K}^{s}):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ can be identified with the factorization ${\bf Sh}(F^{s})\circ {\bf Sh}(i_{F}^{s})$, where ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$ is the full subcategory of ${\cal D}_{K}^{s}$ on the objects of the form $(F(c), S)$ for an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and a $K$-closed sieve $S$ on $F(c)$, $C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}}$ is the Grothendieck topology induced by $C_{K}^{s}$ on ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$, $i_{F}^{s}:({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})\to ({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})$ is the morphism of sites given by the canonical inclusion functor ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}\hookrightarrow {\cal D}_{K}^{s}$, and $F_{s}$ is the morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})$ given by the functor $F$.
nodes.statement_short: The hyperconnected-localic factorization of ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is ${\bf Sh}(F^s)\circ{\bf Sh}(i^s_F)$ through the site ${\cal D}^s_F$ of closed sieves on objects $F(c)$.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the hyperconnected-localic factorization of the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F)\circ {\bf Sh}(i_{K}^{s}):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ can be identified with the factorization ${\bf Sh}(F^{s})\circ {\bf Sh}(i_{F}^{s})$, where ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$ is the full subcategory of ${\cal D}_{K}^{s}$ on the objects of the form $(F(c), S)$ for an object $c$ of $\cal C$ and a $K$-closed sieve $S$ on $F(c)$, $C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}}$ is the Grothendieck topology induced by $C_{K}^{s}$ on ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$, $i_{F}^{s}:({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})\to ({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})$ is the morphism of sites given by the canonical inclusion functor ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}\hookrightarrow {\cal D}_{K}^{s}$, and $F_{s}$ is the morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})$ given by the functor $F$.
nodes.label: thmhyperconnectedlocalicfactorization

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.34
nodes.statement: By Remark \ref{remseparatingsetlocalic}, the topos $\cal G$ arising in the hyperconnected-localic factorization $p'\circ p$ of the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F)$ admits as separating set of objects the family of domains of subobjects of objects of the form ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}(l(c))\cong l'(F(c))$. Now, the full subcategory of ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$ on such objects is equivalent to ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$ by Corollary \ref{corhyperconnectedsieves}, so we have an equivalence $\xi:{\cal G}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})$. The inverse image of the geometric morphism $p:{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)\to {\cal G}$ is precisely the inclusion functor of $\cal G$ into ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$, and the morphism of sites $i_{K}^{s}:({\cal D}, K)\to ({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})$ yields an equivalence ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})\simeq {\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$. So the canonical inclusion functor $i_{F}^{s}$ of ${\cal D}_{F}^{s}$ into ${\cal D}_{K}^{s}$ defines a morphism of sites $({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})\to ({\cal D}_{K}^{s}, C_{K}^{s})$, since it induces the geometric morphism $\xi \circ p\circ {\bf Sh}(i_{K}^{s})$. On the other hand, the inverse image of the geometric morphism $p':{\cal G}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ given by the localic part of the hyperconnected-localic factorization of ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is simply ${\bf Sh}(F)^{\ast}$, regarded as taking values in the subcategory $\cal G$ of ${\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K)$. Therefore the functor $F_{s}$ is a morphism of sites $({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}_{F}^{s}, C_{K}^{s}|_{{\cal D}_{F}^{s}})$ as it induces the geometric morphism $p'\circ \xi^{-1}$. This completes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: The intermediate topos has the subobjects of $l'(F(c))$ as separating set (Remark 6.30), which Corollary 2.16 presents by ${\cal D}^s_F$; identify both legs.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.35 (hyperconnected-localic factorization of interpretations)
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Let ${\mathbb T}_{I}$ be the expansion of $\mathbb T$ whose signature is obtained by adding a predicate symbol $R_{\psi}$ of sorts $I(\vec{x})$ for any context $\vec{x}$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ and any geometric formula $\psi$ in the context $I(\vec{x})$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$, and whose axioms are all the sequents whose image under the extension of $I$ sending each predicate symbol $R_{\psi}$ to the corresponding formula $\{I(\vec{x}). \psi\}$ is provable in $\mathbb S$, and let $I_{s}$ be the obvious interpretation of $\mathbb T$ into ${\mathbb T}_{I}$. Then the hyperconnected-localic factorization of the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ can be identified with the composite ${\bf Sh}(I')\circ {\bf Sh}(I_{s})$.
nodes.statement_short: The factorization for an interpretation passes through the expansion ${\mathbb T}_I$ adding predicates for all image formulae.
assumptions: $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Let ${\mathbb T}_{I}$ be the expansion of $\mathbb T$ whose signature is obtained by adding a predicate symbol $R_{\psi}$ of sorts $I(\vec{x})$ for any context $\vec{x}$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ and any geometric formula $\psi$ in the context $I(\vec{x})$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$, and whose axioms are all the sequents whose image under the extension of $I$ sending each predicate symbol $R_{\psi}$ to the corresponding formula $\{I(\vec{x}). \psi\}$ is provable in $\mathbb S$, and let $I_{s}$ be the obvious interpretation of $\mathbb T$ into ${\mathbb T}_{I}$
conclusions: the hyperconnected-localic factorization of the geometric morphism ${\bf Set }[{\mathbb S}]\to {\bf Set }[{\mathbb T}]$ induced by $I$ can be identified with the composite ${\bf Sh}(I')\circ {\bf Sh}(I_{s})$.
nodes.label: corhyperclocalicintepretation

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.35
nodes.statement: It is immediate to see that the factorization of $I$ as $I_{s}$ followed by $I'$ can be identified with the factorization of $I$, regarded as a morphism of sites $({\cal C}_{\mathbb T}, J_{\mathbb T})\to ({\cal C}_{\mathbb S}, J_{\mathbb S})$, provided by Theorem \ref{thmhyperconnectedlocalicfactorization} by using Proposition \ref{propcoverreflecting}, Corollary \ref{corinterpretationsfaithful} and Remark \ref{remsubcanonicalclosedsubobjects}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the factorization with that of Theorem 6.34.

nodes.name: Remark 6.36 (generalizes Theories, Sites, Toposes 7.1.3)
nodes.statement: Corollary \ref{corhyperclocalicintepretation} generalizes the corresponding result for expansions of theories proved as Theorem 7.1.3 in \cite{OCBook}.
nodes.statement_short: Generalizes the result for expansions in Caramello's book.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.37 (alternative criterion for flat functors inducing equivalences)
nodes.statement: Let $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$. Then $f$ is an equivalence if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $F$ is cover-reflecting; \item for every subobject $A\rightarrowtail F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$; \item the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A $J$-continuous flat functor induces an equivalence iff it is cover-reflecting, subobjects of $F(c)$ come from sieves, and its image is separating.
assumptions: $({\cal C}, J)$ be a small-generated site, $\cal E$ a Grothendieck topos and $F:{\cal C}\to {\cal E}$ a $J$-continuous flat functor inducing a geometric morphism $f:{\cal E}\to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$
conclusions: $f$ is an equivalence if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $F$ is cover-reflecting; \item for every subobject $A\rightarrowtail F(c)$ in $\cal E$ there exists a ($J$-closed) sieve $R$ on $c$ such that $A$ is the union of the images of the arrows $F(f)$ for $f\in R$; \item the objects of the form $F(c)$ for $c\in {\cal C}$ form a separating set for the topos $\cal E$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corflatequivalence2

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.37
nodes.statement: The functor $f^{\ast}$ is one half of an equivalence of categories if and only if it is full and faithful and essentially surjective. Since faithfulness and closure of its image under subobjects implies fullness for the functor $f^{\ast}$, we conclude that $f^{\ast}$ is one half of an equivalence if and only if it is faithful, essentially surjective and its image is closed under subobjects. Our thesis thus follows from Propositions \ref{propcoverreflecting}, \ref{prophypersubobjects} and \ref{propessentiallysurjective}.
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence = faithful, essentially surjective, subobject-closed image; apply Propositions 6.1, 6.22, 6.26.

nodes.name: Comparison of the two equivalence criteria for flat functors
nodes.statement: It is interesting to compare this characterization with the different, but equivalent, criterion provided by Corollary \ref{flatequivalence}: the difference lies in condition (ii) of Corollary \ref{corflatequivalence2} which is replaced by the ``local fullness'' condition of Corollary \ref{flatequivalence}.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 6.37 differs from Corollary 5.11 by replacing local fullness with a subobject condition.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.38 (interpretations inducing Morita equivalences)
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Then $I$ induces a Morita-equivalence between $\mathbb T$ and $\mathbb S$ if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for every sequent $\sigma$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$, if the sequent $I(\sigma)$ is provable in $\mathbb S$ then $\sigma$ is provable in $\mathbb T$; \item the image of $I$ is closed under subobjects (that is, for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula of the form $I(\phi)$ for a geometric formula $\phi$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$); \item for every sort $B$ of the signature of $\mathbb S$, the object $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: An interpretation induces a Morita equivalence iff it reflects provability, has subobject-closed image, and sorts are covered by its image.
assumptions: $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$
conclusions: $I$ induces a Morita-equivalence between $\mathbb T$ and $\mathbb S$ if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item for every sequent $\sigma$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$, if the sequent $I(\sigma)$ is provable in $\mathbb S$ then $\sigma$ is provable in $\mathbb T$; \item the image of $I$ is closed under subobjects (that is, for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula of the form $I(\phi)$ for a geometric formula $\phi$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$); \item for every sort $B$ of the signature of $\mathbb S$, the object $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corsyntacticMorita

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.38
nodes.statement: Our thesis immediately follows from Corollaries \ref{corinterpretationsfaithful} and \ref{corsyntactichyperconnected}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Corollaries 6.2 and 6.24.

nodes.name: Remark 6.39 (equivalence onto its image)
nodes.statement: Conditions (i) and (ii) of Corollary \ref{corsyntacticMorita} can be reformulated as the requirement that the functor $I$ should be an equivalence onto its image.
nodes.statement_short: Conditions (i),(ii) say $I$ is an equivalence onto its image.

nodes.name: Example 6.40 (MV-algebras and lattice-ordered groups with strong unit)
nodes.statement: Corollary \ref{corsyntacticMorita} can for instance be applied to the interpretation of the algebraic theory $\mathbb{MV}$ of MV-algebras into the theory ${\mathbb L}_{u}$ of lattice-ordered abelian groups with strong unit established in \cite{OC17}, which, as proved in $\cite{OC17}$, induces a Morita equivalence. Condition (iii) is satisfied since the formula $\{x. \top\}$ is covered in ${\cal C}_{{\mathbb L}_{u}}$ by the objects in the image of $I$. Indeed, by the axiom expressing the property of strong unit, the arrows $\{x'. 0\leq x'\leq u\}\to \{x. \top\}$ given by $x=nx'$ (for $n\in {\mathbb Z}$) generate a $J_{{\mathbb L}_{u}}$-covering sieve. One can also understand concretely why condition (ii) is satisfied; indeed, by using the construction of the $\ell$-group associated with an MV-algebra in terms of good sequences of elements of the latter, one can prove that for every atomic formula $\chi(\vec{x})$ over the signature of ${\mathbb L}_{u}$, there exists a Horn formula $\chi^{MV}(\vec{x})$ in the same context over the signature of $\mathbb{MV}$ such that the formula $I(\chi^{MV}(\vec{x}))$ is provably equivalent in ${\mathbb L}_{u}$ (in the context $\vec{x}$) to the formula $\chi \wedge (0\leq \vec{x} \leq u)$.
nodes.statement_short: The interpretation of MV-algebras into $\ell$-groups with strong unit satisfies the conditions, recovering a Morita equivalence.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.41 (alternative criterion for morphisms of sites inducing equivalences)
nodes.statement: Let $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites. Then the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is an equivalence if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting, closed-sieve-lifting and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} (recall that, if $K$ is subcanonical, the latter condition is equivalent to $F$ being $K$-dense).
nodes.statement_short: ${\bf Sh}(F)$ is an equivalence iff $F$ is cover-reflecting, closed-sieve-lifting and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition 5.5.
assumptions: $F:({\cal C}, J)\to ({\cal D}, K)$ be a morphism of small-generated sites
conclusions: the geometric morphism ${\bf Sh}(F):{\bf Sh}({\cal D}, K) \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)$ induced by $F$ is an equivalence if and only if $F$ is cover-reflecting, closed-sieve-lifting and satisfies condition (ii) of Proposition \ref{propweaklydensemorphism} (recall that, if $K$ is subcanonical, the latter condition is equivalent to $F$ being $K$-dense).
nodes.label: corquivalencesites

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.41
nodes.statement: Since a geometric morphism $f$ is an equivalence if and only if it is hyperconnected and its inverse image is essentially surjective, the thesis follows from Proposition \ref{propessentialsurjectivitysites} and Theorem \ref{Morphismsmaalgenerated}(a).
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence = hyperconnected with essentially surjective inverse image; apply Proposition 6.28 and Theorem 6.3.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.42 (inclusions via local surjectivity and subobject closure)
nodes.statement: Let $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be a geometric morphism. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $f$ is an inclusion if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective and its image is closed under subobjects. \item $f$ is an equivalence if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful, locally surjective and its image is closed under subobjects. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is an inclusion iff $f^*$ is locally surjective with subobject-closed image; an equivalence iff moreover faithful.
assumptions: $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal E}$ be a geometric morphism
conclusions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $f$ is an inclusion if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective and its image is closed under subobjects. \item $f$ is an equivalence if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is faithful, locally surjective and its image is closed under subobjects. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: corinclusionequivalence2

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.42
nodes.statement: As observed in the proof of Corollary \ref{corinclusionequivalence}, $f$ is an inclusion if and only if the morphism of sites $f^{\ast}:({\cal E}, ({J_{\cal E}^{\textup{can}}})_{f^{\ast}})\to ({\cal F}, J_{\cal F}^{\textup{can}})$ is dense (equivalently, weakly dense). Now, this morphism is $ J_{\cal F}^{\textup{can}}$-dense if and only if $f^{\ast}$ is locally surjective (in the sense of Corollary \ref{corinclusionequivalence}(i)), while it is closed-sieve-lifting if and only if the image of $f^{\ast}$ is closed under subobjects; indeed, for any Grothendieck topology $K$ on a Grothendieck topos $\cal G$ containing the canonical one, any $K$-closed sieve is equal to the principal sieve on a subobject. This proves the first part of the corollary; the second part follows from the first by using that a geometric morphism is an equivalence if and only if it is both a surjection and an inclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Corollary 6.41 to $f^*$ as a morphism of sites, translating density and closed-sieve-lifting.

nodes.name: Slice topos ${\bf Sh}({\cal C},J)/a_J(P)\simeq{\bf Sh}(\int P,J_P)$ (SGA4 III 5.4)
nodes.statement: Given a small-generated site $({\cal C}, J)$ and a presheaf $P:{\cal C}^{\textup{op}}\to {\bf Set }$, let us deduce, as a consequence of Corollary \ref{corflatequivalence2}, that we have an equivalence of toposes \[ {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\slash a_{J}(P)\simeq {\bf Sh}(\textstyle \int P, J_{P}), \] where $\int P$ is the category of elements of $P$ and $J_{P}$ is the Grothendieck topology on $\int P$ whose covering sieves are the sieves which are sent by the canonical projection $\pi_{P}:\int P \to {\cal C}$ to $J$-covering families. This equivalence, which was already established in Proposition III 5.4 \cite{grothendieck}, is induced by the (flat) $J_{P}$-continuous functor $F_{P}:\int P \to {\bf Sh}({\cal C}, J)\slash a_{J}(P)$ sending any object $(c, s)$ of $\int P$ to the image under $a_{J}$ of the arrow $y_{\cal C}(c)\to P$ induced by $(c, x)$ via the Yoneda lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The slice of a sheaf topos over $a_J(P)$ is equivalent to sheaves on the category of elements of $P$ with the induced topology.

nodes.name: Proof of the slice equivalence
nodes.statement_short: $F_P$ is flat and $J_P$ is its induced topology; check the conditions of Corollary 6.37: images separate and subobjects come from sieves.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.43 (characterization of quotient interpretations)
nodes.statement: Let $I:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ be an interpretation of a geometric theory $\mathbb T$ into a geometric theory ${\mathbb S}$. Then $I$ is isomorphic (over ${\cal C}_{\mathbb T}$) to the canonical interpretation $I_{\mathbb T}^{{\mathbb T}'}:{\cal C}_{\mathbb T}\to {\cal C}_{{\mathbb T}'}$ of ${\mathbb T}$ into a quotient ${\mathbb T}'$ of ${\mathbb T}$ if and only if it satisfies the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The image of $I$ is closed under subobjects (that is, for any sorts $A_{1}, \ldots, A_{n}$ of the signature of $\mathbb T$, every geometric formula $\psi$ over the signature of $\mathbb S$ in the context $I((x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}}))$ is $\mathbb T$-provably equivalent (in its context) to a formula of the form $I(\phi)$ for a geometric formula $\phi$ over the signature of $\mathbb T$ in the context $(x_{1}^{A_{1}}, \ldots, x_{n}^{A_{n}})$). \item For every sort $B$ of the signature of $\mathbb S$, the object $\{x^{B}. \top\}$ is $J_{\mathbb S}$-covered by objects in the image of $I$. \end{enumerate} Condition (i) can be equivalently replaced by the following condition : \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item[(i)'] For every objects $\{\vec{x}. \phi\}$ and $\{\vec{y}. \psi\}$ of ${\cal C}_{\mathbb T}$ and any $\mathbb S$-provably functional formula $\theta(I(\vec{x}), I(\vec{y}))$ from $I(\{\vec{x}. \phi\})$ to $I(\{\vec{y}. \psi\})$ there exist a set of $\mathbb T$-provably functional formulae $\{\chi_{i}(\vec{x_i}, \vec{x}) \}:\{\vec{x_i}. \phi_{i}\}\to \{\vec{x}. \phi\}$ such that the sequent $(I(\phi) \vdash_{I(\vec{x})} \mathbin{\mathop{\textup{\huge $\vee$}}\limits_{i}}(\exists I(\vec{x_{i}}) I(\chi_{i}(\vec{x_i}, \vec{x})))$ is provable in $\mathbb S$ and $\mathbb T$-provably functional formulae $\xi_{i}(\vec{x_i}, \vec{y}):\{\vec{x_i}. \phi_{i}\} \to \{\vec{y}. \psi\}$ (for each $i$) such that $[\theta]\circ I([\chi_{i}])=I([\xi_{i}])$ in ${\cal C}_{\mathbb S}$ (i.e. the bi-sequent $((\exists I(\vec{x}))(\theta \wedge I([\chi_i])) \dashv \vdash_{I(\vec{x_{i}})} I([\xi_{i}]))$ is provable in $\mathbb S$). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: An interpretation is isomorphic to the canonical interpretation into a quotient iff its image is subobject-closed (or locally full) and covers all sorts.
